data.name: Kartikeya
data.gender_notes: Kartikeya is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The God with six faces, the son of Shiva, who led the army of gods in battles against the demons. The name Kartikeya carries the meaning “God of War” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Tamil, Telugu. Parents who choose Kartikeya usually hope their child will grow to embody god of war and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the power of will and determination, and the ability to overcome challenges and adversities.
data.etymology: Kartikeya belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of War.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kartikeya total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: Kartikeya is an important deity in Hindu mythology, known as the God of War and the God of strong desire, particularly in Tamil Nadu and other parts of South India. He is the commander of the divine army during the great cosmic churning of the ocean. In popular culture, Kartikeya is also revered as the God of beauty, youth, art, and sensuality. His festival, known as Kartik Purnima or Skanda Sashti, is celebrated with utmost devotion across India.
data.spiritual_significance: Kartikeya represents self-motivated action and spiritual growth through overcoming obstacles. As a warrior, he embodies courage, loyalty, and discipline. Worshipping Kartikeya can bring protection, spiritual enlightenment, and the capacity to face life's challenges with courage and determination. Additionally, he is believed to grant happiness, peace, and blessings for those who seek his blessings sincerely.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kartikeya is the god of war and son of Shiva and Parvati. He is also known as Murugan or Subramanian. He is the leader of armies of gods, symbolizing courage, valor, and victory over evil. Kartikeya's mount is a peacock, representing beauty and grace in the midst of battle.

vedic_reference.note: Kartikeya is a significant deity in Hinduism, mentioned in various Hindu scriptures like the Mahabharata, the Puranas, and the Agni Purana. He is also known as Murugan in Tamil Nadu, Subrahmanya in Karnataka, and Skanda in other parts of India.

historical_references.reference: Kartikeya is also known as Murugan and Skanda. He is the god of war, peace, and victory in the Hindu pantheon. Kartikeya is the son of Shiva and Parvati and is considered the younger brother of Ganesha. The story of Kartikeya's birth is described in various Hindu scriptures. According to one account, when Shiva was meditating on Mount Kailash, Parvati created Kartikeya from a spark of her body to protect Shiva from the demon Taraka.

Another belief about the origin of Kartikeya is found in the Skanda Purana, one of the eighteen major Puranas in Hinduism. It mentions that Shiva and Parvati decided to bring Kartikeya to life to lead an army of gods against the demon Surapena. Parvati created the six faces and two arms of Kartikeya and bathed him in the sacred waters of the Ganga, Saraswati, and Godavari rivers.
historical_references.time_period: Medieval India, around 7th to 10th Century CE
